title: Why New Jersey Is America's Luckiest Lottery State
text:
As a $1 billion Powerball jackpot drove brisk ticket sales in Edison, New Jersey, lottery officials and local workers highlighted a statistical trend on August 12, 2026: the state punches above its weight class for major winners, anchored by multi-million dollar payouts at a single suburban storefront.
Inside the Hot Streak at Quick Stop Convenience Queues formed quickly at the counter as players chased the nine-figure prize. Workers at the Quick Stop Convenience store in Edison reported an immediate surge in foot traffic leading up to the evening drawing, fueled by local lore that treats the shop as a regional talisman for unexpected wealth.
That reputation is built on recent history. The store recently sold a winning ticket worth more than $200 million. For patrons skeptical that lightning might strike the same address twice, lottery records show the exact same location subsequently sold a ticket worth another $5 million.
“The people say it’s a very lucky store,” said Quick Stop convenience store worker Ricky Patel.
Statewide Numbers Back the Winning Reputation The concentration of wealth at single retail locations reflects a broader statewide pattern tracked by the New Jersey Lottery. State officials note that New Jersey has produced significant lottery wins over recent years, according to data from the New Jersey Lottery.
Data provided by lottery administrators show that at least six Mega Millions winners have emerged from the state since 2018, including a separate $1 billion top-prize winner. Over that exact same timeframe, New Jersey players claimed five major Powerball wins.
Within the past year alone, at least 75 players across New Jersey have claimed individual prizes valued at $1 million or higher, according to state figures.
The Long-Term Economic Ripple of Multi-Million Dollar Payouts As the numbers from Edison demonstrate, the allure of historic jackpots continues to drive robust ticket sales across New Jersey neighborhoods, reinforcing the state’s reputation for high-stakes lottery history.
